title: O, What Amazing Words of Grace
description: O, What Amazing Words of Grace in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Samuel Medley wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 264 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Fountain of Living Waters”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, what a-ma-zing words of grace Are in the gos-pel found! Suit-ed to ev-ery sin-ner's case, Who hears the joy-ful sound.

lines: O, what amazing words of grace
Come, then, with all your wants and wounds;
This spring with living water flows,
Come, thirsty souls, your wants disclose,

licence: Public domain: Samuel Medley died in 1799.
credits: Words by Samuel Medley (1738–1799), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
